To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the combination of ETD and CRCIDs can be used as a starting scan to characterize enzymatically digested peptides from complex proteins.

the combination of CID, ETD, and CID of an ion isolated from ETD (i.e., CRCID) provides complementary information for the characterization of large peptides from complex proteins at the low femtomo level.

we have expanded our previous LC-MS platform, ERPA, to include ETD and CRCIDs to improve the characterization of large peptides from complex proteins, and that the new strategy is a useful tool to characterize enzymatic peptides over a broad range (e.g., 500-5000 Da) of masses using LCMS with data-dependent acquisitions.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of a new LC-MS approach that combines collision-induced dissociation, electron-transfer dissociation, and CID of an ion isolated after charge-reduced dissociation to characterize large peptides and complex proteins with post-transcriptional modifications.
the development of an on-line LC-ETD-CID approach for the characterization of large peptides from complex proteins.
the analysis of complex protein mixtures
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the new platform is a good starting approach for the characterization of complex proteins, and it can be used as a guide for subsequent experiments.

the combination of the three activation methods, ETD, CID-MS2, and CRCID-MS2, provides a more comprehensive and conclusive characterization of large peptide fragments than any of the three activation steps alone.
this new LC-MS approach provides an efficient and sensitive platform for the characterization of large peptides and complex proteins.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed an LC-MS approach to characterize complex proteins at the low femtome level.

the new LC-MS approach can be used to determine sites of modification (e.g., phosphorylation and glycoproteins) and the peptide sequence for large peptides (i.e., >or=2000 Da) from complex mixtures at the low femtogram (or low femtomol) level.

the combination of the three activation steps, ETD, CID, and CRCID, provides a more robust approach for the characterization of post-translational modification sites and the sequence of large peptides, especially for the low femtomole range.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a new LC-MS method can be developed by combining different activation methods, such as CID, ETD, and CID of charge-reduced species.
ETD is not only useful for the characterization of small peptides, but it can also be applied to the characterization of large peptides and proteins.
the new LC-MS strategy can be applied for the characterization of complex proteins with a variety of posttranslational modifications.
